newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar reverses to end at one-week high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar reverses to end at one-week high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended up and at a one-week high Wednesday as industry-linked buying helped the market snap back from a brush with six-month lows, traders said.

The market sagged early in the session, touching off sell stops below 10.29 cents a lb for March delivery. But buyers returned to the market after March managed to hold key support at 10.21 cents, a low from late April.
Scale-down buying from the trade provided an underpinning, while short covering by commodity funds at the highs lifted the market to its best settlement in a week.
"We bounced off the low of 10.21, and the trade started to buy it," said one broker. The intraday reversal could signal a floor to the recent downtrend, he added.
New York raw have slid more than a cent per pound in the past two months, hurt by growing signs of a large world supply surplus for the 1996/97 crop year.
"We might have seen a low, and funds may start to lighten up on their short positions," the trader said.
March ended 0.07 firmer at 10.40 after trading from 10.21 to 10.43. Second-position May gained 0.04 to 10.48, while the outer months increased 0.02 to 0.03 cent.
Today's positive finish sent a technically constructive signal, dealers said, but with producers eager to lock in prices toward 10.50 cents, additional gains would be hard to come by.
The day's volume reached an estimated 12,962 lots.
